problem: Embodied Question Answering (EQA) systems re-explore familiar environments for every question and do not retain spatial memory or use user feedback, which limits practicality in real deployments.
motivation: Real-world home robots operate repeatedly in the same environment, so they should store what they have seen and reuse it instead of exploring again. The paper draws on cognition-inspired spatial memory and on the intermediate features of vision-language models (VLMs) to build such a memory. It also needs reliable place recognition to localize against that memory.
key_idea: Build a cognition-inspired cognitive map from intermediate VLM features so a robot can navigate, answer questions, store environment information, and globally localize, backed by a zero-shot ViT-based place recognition method (ViTPR).
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract claims that intermediate VLM features can serve both as spatial memory for question answering and as a basis for localization. It also claims that ViTPR reaches state-of-the-art zero-shot VPR on Nordland.
method: EnvQA task: extends EQA by adding persistent spatial memory and user feedback, so the robot avoids repeated exploration of a known environment.
Cognitive map: cognition-inspired memory that stores environment information using intermediate features of VLMs.
EnvQA system: autonomously navigates, answers queries, and writes new environment information into the map.
ViTPR: zero-shot image-image matching with large-scale vision transformers for visual place recognition and global localization.
